definition: Software that prevents tracking technologies from collecting user data by blocking tracking scripts, cookies, and other surveillance mechanisms on websites.
metaDescription: Learn about tracker blockers - privacy tools that block tracking scripts and prevent websites from collecting your personal data online.
simpleExplanation: Think of a tracker blocker as a security guard for your web browsing. It stops invisible tracking scripts from following you around the internet, collecting information about what you do, where you go, and what you're interested in online.
whyItMatters: Tracker blockers protect your privacy by preventing companies from building detailed profiles about your online behavior. They also improve browsing speed and reduce data usage by blocking unnecessary tracking code.
technicalDetail: Tracker blockers use filter lists and heuristics to identify and block tracking domains, scripts, and pixels. They can operate at the browser level through extensions, at the DNS level, or as standalone applications that filter network traffic before it reaches your browser.

examples.explanation: Installing uBlock Origin or Ghostery in your browser to automatically block tracking scripts from Google Analytics, Facebook pixels, and advertising networks across all websites you visit.
Using Pi-hole on your home network to block tracking domains for all devices connected to your WiFi, preventing smart TVs, phones, and computers from sending data to trackers.
Firefox's Enhanced Tracking Protection automatically blocks cross-site trackers, social media trackers, and fingerprinting scripts without requiring additional software installation.
